blockers.what: Edit > Cut/Copy/Paste (lines 83-85) and Undo/Redo (lines 75-81) are built with custom `click` handlers plus the accelerators CmdOrCtrl+X / +C / +V / +Z / (Shift+CmdOrCtrl+Z | Ctrl+Y), instead of Electron's `role: 'cut' | 'copy' | 'paste' | 'undo' | 'redo'`. The click handler (line 30, `logAction`) only `console.log`s. Verified by evaluating `buildAppMenuTemplate` against a stubbed `electron` module: every one of the five items comes back `{ role: undefined, accelerator: <set>, hasClick: true }`.
blockers.why: `installAppMenu()` now runs on `whenReady` (src/main/index.ts:52), so these become live OS application-menu accelerators. The native menu consumes the keystroke before it reaches the focused webContents, so the clipboard and undo shortcuts stop working inside the renderer's only text input — the chat composer textarea (`#chat-composer`, src/renderer/src/components/ChatPanel.tsx:28), which this same PR ships and which the PR's own recording shows being typed into. This is a regression, not just a gap: before this PR no application menu was set, so Electron installed its default menu whose Edit items carry the proper roles and clipboard worked. `autoHideMenuBar: true` (removed at src/main/index.ts:15) only hid that menu; its accelerators were still live. It also contradicts 80-roadmap.md, which scopes M0.4 to "Static UI, no logic" and schedules `feat: File/Edit menus with OS accelerators + clipboard` at M5.1 — the accelerators arrived four milestones early, wired to no-ops.
blockers.fix: For M0.4 use roles for the whole clipboard/history group: `{ role: 'undo' }, { role: 'redo' }, { type: 'separator' }, { role: 'cut' }, { role: 'copy' }, { role: 'paste' }` (or simply `{ role: 'editMenu' }`), and keep the placeholder `item(...)` no-ops for the `file.*` entries only. When history lands, replace just Undo/Redo with main-side handlers driven by `history.canUndo/canRedo` per 10-architecture.md §5. Alternatively, drop the accelerator argument from the Edit items until M5.1 so no keystroke is captured.

majors.what: `MENU_ACTIONS` and the derived `MenuAction` union are declared in the main process. 10-architecture.md §2 declares the wire contract as `'app:menu': MenuAction` and names `src/shared/ipc-contract.ts` the "source of truth"; that file (src/shared/ipc-contract.ts:19) still types the event as `{ action: string }` and this PR does not update it.
majors.why: Contradicts a plan doc without updating it, and splits the vocabulary permanently: the renderer may not import from `src/main/**` (.oxlintrc.json no-restricted-imports override), so when `app:menu` is actually wired the renderer will have to redeclare the same ten action ids, and the shared contract will keep validating them as an unconstrained `string`. The comment at line 8 ("become the `app:menu` event payload (see src/shared/ipc-contract.ts)") points at a file that does not contain them — a comment that is already drifted on the day it lands.
majors.fix: Move `MENU_ACTIONS` / `MenuAction` into `src/shared/ipc-contract.ts` and narrow `IpcEvents['app:menu']` to `{ action: MenuAction }`; import the type back into appMenu.ts. `src/shared` stays dependency-free (a const string array plus a derived union), so this respects the direction rule.

majors.what: The six new shell components are placed in a flat `src/renderer/src/components/` bucket (AppShell, Canvas, ChatPanel, MenuTabStrip, StatusBar, ThumbnailRail). 10-architecture.md §1.3 prescribes `app/App.tsx` for the shell layout and `features/<feature>/<Component>.tsx` for each region (`features/deck/ThumbnailRail.tsx`, `features/canvas/SlideCanvas.tsx`, `features/chat/ChatPanel.tsx`, `features/format/FormatBar.tsx`, `features/statusbar/StatusBar.tsx`), and reserves `components/ui/*` for shadcn-vendored primitives only.
majors.why: Contradicts the architecture doc without updating it, and the bucket it creates is the one path the doc reserves for something else — so vendoring the first shadcn primitive will land feature components and UI primitives in the same directory. Six files plus every import site have to move later, and the longer the shell grows the more expensive that is. (The extra `src/renderer/src/` nesting is pre-existing from the PR #2 scaffold and is not this PR's doing.)
majors.fix: Move each region under `src/renderer/src/features/{ribbon,format,thumbnails,canvas,chat,statusbar}/` and the frame into `app/AppShell.tsx`, or amend 10-architecture.md §1.3 in this PR to record the flat layout as the deliberate decision.

majors.what: `buildAppMenuTemplate` is exported — evidently factored out to be testable — but nothing tests it, and as written it cannot be tested: the module imports `app` and `Menu` from `electron` at top level (line 2), which does not resolve in the Vitest node environment. `tests/unit/` contains no app-menu test.
majors.why: 70-testing-ci.md §0 makes this the load-bearing rule of the repo: "CI runs unit tests and lint only ... No Electron", and "testability pressure pushes logic into pure functions" so that "Electron code becomes a thin, boring shell". The menu template is exactly that kind of pure data — a table of labels, action ids and accelerators — and it is currently invisible to CI. Concretely, a test asserting the role/accelerator table is what would have caught the blocker above; I had to alias `electron` to a stub in a throwaway Vitest config to inspect it at all.
majors.fix: Keep the builder electron-free: `import type { MenuItemConstructorOptions } from 'electron'` only, and take `{ platform, appName }` as parameters instead of reading `process.platform` / `app.name` inside. Leave the `electron` value imports in `installAppMenu`. Then add `tests/unit/app-menu.test.ts` asserting, for both `'darwin'` and `'win32'`, that every id in `MENU_ACTIONS` is reachable exactly once and that the clipboard/history items carry roles rather than bare accelerators.

minors.what: Nit: "Align left" and "Align right" both render the glyph `≡`; only "Align center" differs (`≣`, line 100). Visible in the committed screenshot at docs/media/m04-app-shell.png — the first and third align buttons are indistinguishable.
minors.why: The wireframe's ASCII `≡ ≣ ≡` was transcribed literally; on screen it reads as a broken control group.
minors.fix: Use distinct marks (e.g. small inline SVGs like the Image button already uses, or `≡` / `≣` / `≢` with differing justification), or drop the align group until it is wired.

minors.what: Nit: the Font and Font-size `<select>`s carry `aria-disabled="true"` (lines 65, 75) but remain fully operable — a user can change the value and nothing happens.
minors.why: Unlike the buttons, where `aria-disabled` is a deliberate focusable-but-inert choice, a select that announces as disabled and then changes state is an accessibility lie.
minors.fix: Either add `disabled`, or drop `aria-disabled` and keep them cosmetic-only.

minors.what: Nit: `role="tab"` / `aria-selected="true"` with no `aria-controls` and no element with `role="tabpanel"` anywhere in the shell.
minors.why: An incomplete tab pattern; screen readers announce a tab that controls nothing.
minors.fix: Add `aria-controls` pointing at the toolbar (which is the panel this tab governs) and give the toolbar `role="tabpanel"` plus an id, or drop the tablist roles until a second tab exists.

minors.what: Nit: a 227 KB `.webm` and a 38 KB `.png` are committed into the repo. 70-testing-ci.md §7.3 says a UI PR "attaches a short screencast (GIF or mp4)"; `main` has no `docs/` directory at all, so `docs/media/` is a new convention introduced here, in a format outside the stated two.
minors.why: Per-milestone binaries committed to git accumulate permanently and cannot be pruned; the rule as written points at PR attachments instead.
minors.fix: Attach the recording to the PR description (GitHub hosts it) rather than committing it, or add a short note to 70-testing-ci.md §7.3 establishing `docs/media/` and webm as the convention.

minors.what: Nit: `fireEvent.click(slide3 as HTMLButtonElement)` casts away the `null` that line 47 just asserted against; and the "keeps every formatting control inert" case (line 60) only walks `getAllByRole('button')`, so the two `<select>`s escape it.
minors.why: Small honesty gaps in an otherwise good test file — the cast hides the narrowing, and the inert assertion does not actually cover every control it claims to.
minors.fix: Use `assert(slide3 instanceof HTMLButtonElement)` or `screen.getByRole('button', { name: /Slide 3/ })`; extend the inert loop over `[...getAllByRole('button'), ...getAllByRole('combobox')]`.

minors.what: Nit: the commit/PR title is 92 characters; 70-testing-ci.md §7.1 caps it at 72 (80-roadmap.md's own M0.4 title is 62). The changeset is ~600 lines excluding lockfile and media against §7.4's "< 400 changed lines" target.
minors.why: Both are stated conventions the repo has otherwise followed.
minors.fix: Retitle to the roadmap's own wording: `feat: app shell layout (menu bar, thumbnail rail, canvas, status bar)`.

All three are green, so nothing is masked; 67 of the 71 tests belong to M1.1 and no failure needed attribution. package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml also carry M1.1's edits in the tree; the dependency review below is against `gh pr diff 3` only.
verification.not_run: Electron itself was never launched (headless WSL, no display). The blocker's template shape was verified programmatically; the behavioural consequence (native menu accelerators pre-empting the focused webContents) rests on documented Electron semantics, not on an observed run. This is the single largest source of residual uncertainty in this verdict.

hypotheses_tested: H1: the Edit menu's custom click handlers hijack the clipboard accelerators from the chat textarea. CONFIRMED (blocker). Ran buildAppMenuTemplate under Vitest with `electron` aliased to a stub: Cut/Copy/Paste/Undo/Redo all return role=undefined with accelerators CmdOrCtrl+X/C/V/Z and a click handler that only logs. Firing the Paste item's click yields exactly `['edit.paste']` and no clipboard effect. ChatPanel.tsx:28 renders the textarea that is affected.
H2: PR #3 touches or worsens the unchecked `shell.openExternal` in src/main/index.ts. REJECTED — see openExternal_note below.

H3: the tsconfig include split (`tests/unit/**/*` -> `*.ts` in node + `*.tsx` in web) silently drops a test file from typechecking. REJECTED — both projects typecheck clean, every file under tests/unit/ is matched by exactly one project, and the .tsx test needs the web project's DOM lib and `jsx: react-jsx` which the node project lacks. The split is the right fix, not a dodge.

H4: `useState(1)` in AppShell dereferences or misreports when the deck is empty. REJECTED for now — slideCount is the module constant PLACEHOLDER_SLIDE_COUNT = 3 (AppShell.tsx:10) and ThumbnailRail maps over `Array.from({length: slideCount})`, so 0 renders an empty list and the status bar would read "Slide 1 of 0". Latent only; unreachable in M0.4 and this state is replaced wholesale by M1.1. Not raised.

H5: React identity churn defeats the `memo` on ThumbnailCard. REJECTED — `onSelectSlide` is a `useCallback` with an empty dep array (AppShell.tsx:21) and `number`/`selected` are primitives, so only the two cards whose `selected` flips re-render on a selection change.

H6: the change introduces an unvalidated trust boundary — new IPC channel, iframe, innerHTML, or filesystem path. REJECTED — the diff adds no `ipcMain.handle`, no `webContents.send`, no `<iframe>`, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no `fs` access, and no new `any` / `as unknown as` / non-null `!`. The index.html CSP and the `webPreferences` block (sandbox/contextIsolation/nodeIntegration/webviewTag) are byte-identical to main.

H7: the new devDependencies violate the dependency policy. REJECTED — 11-tech-stack.md line 73 already sanctions `@testing-library/react` at `^16.3`; `@testing-library/dom` is its required peer; both are dev-only, pure JS, non-native, absent from the catalog (so caret is the correct pin per the "caret for leaf libraries" rule). `happy-dom`, `@vitejs/plugin-react` and `playwright` were all already declared (playwright in experiments/init/harness/package.json, which record-shell.mjs uses).
notes.openExternal_note: PRE-EXISTING, NOT TOUCHED, NOT WORSENED — recorded here rather than as a finding against this PR. src/main/index.ts:31-34 passes an arbitrary URL straight to `shell.openExternal(url)` from `setWindowOpenHandler` with no scheme allow-list; the electron-security-checklist §4/§10 rates that a blocker in general. It arrived in the scaffold (commit 200adf5, PR #2). PR #3's three hunks against this file are lines 1-3 (the appMenu import), line 15 (`autoHideMenuBar: true -> false`) and line 52 (`installAppMenu()` in whenReady) — the handler body is unchanged, and nothing in the diff creates a new path that can reach it (the shell renders no anchors and no iframe). Fix when the area is next touched: `const u = new URL(url); if (u.protocol !== 'https:' && u.protocol !== 'http:') return { action: 'deny' }` before `void shell.openExternal(url)`, plus the still-missing `will-navigate` cancel handler.
notes.plan_doc_conflicts_not_raised: 70-testing-ci.md §2.2 says component DOM assertions are out of scope beyond "smoke-mounting a couple of critical surfaces", §2.3 asks for colocated `src/renderer/**/*.test.tsx`, and §2.1 specifies `environment: 'jsdom'`. I did not raise these: the shell is fairly described as a critical surface being smoke-mounted, `tests/unit/` was established by the PR #2 scaffold rather than by this PR, and happy-dom is explicitly endorsed by 11-tech-stack.md line 72 — 70 and 11 contradict each other, which is a doc bug and not this PR's. The 20-ui-wireframes.md spec is met faithfully: Home-only tab strip, the exact toolbar row, the exact status-bar fields (position / theme / issues / session cost / Present), and the File and Edit menu trees item-for-item.

notes.summary: The layout work itself is genuinely good: faithful to 20-ui-wireframes.md, correctly memoized, no trust boundaries touched, and the four component tests pin real behaviour rather than smoke-mounting. The problem is the part of the change that is not layout — installing an Electron application menu whose Edit items bind CmdOrCtrl+X/C/V/Z to console.log no-ops, which takes the clipboard away from the chat composer this same PR ships, and does so four milestones ahead of the roadmap entry that was supposed to build it. Swapping those five items to Electron roles is a one-line-each fix; the three majors (contract location, component placement, an untestable main-process module) are cheap now and expensive after the shell grows.
